project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Catalogue-addition settlement gate. Nearby attractions, estates, ports and neighbouring settlements do not inflate the place score. Score corrected after removal of the artificial sub-60 catalogue gate. Settlement merit was assessed before applying the map threshold; standalone attractions were not transferred into the town score. Angus-wide full audit completed 2026-09-01: all six visitor categories, the four named commercial trail providers, current official/conventional routes, strict-boundary scoring and local HES/NRHE integrity were checked.

features.shortDescription: 8-21 (INCLUSIVE NOS) FISHTOWN OF USAN WITH LOOKOUT TOWER (1 OF 2)
features.reviewNotes: Imported from the HES national Listed Buildings spatial data. Statutory listing and location are authoritative; construction-date review remains separate. NRHE record linked by matching point location; review if it represents a distinct asset.
features.fullDescription: Mid 19th century. Single storey row originally of 14 cottages, now derelict, with 4-stage lookout tower to off-centre left. Rubble with raised ashlar margins, some timber lintels to window embrasures. Tower rising out of pitched roof gear shed, harled, with round-arched bipartite windows to each face at different stages above ground, and with oculuc to S elevation at 4th stage, below crenellated wallhead parapet with billeted corbel course and red brick stacks (?) to 2 corners.

features.reviewNotes: Imported from the HES national Listed Buildings spatial data. Statutory listing and location are authoritative; construction-date review remains separate. NRHE record linked by matching point location; review if it represents a distinct asset.
features.fullDescription: Late 19th century. 2-stage, pyramidally-roofed, lookout tower and residence. Pink stugged sandstone squared and snecked, near square in plan, sited at corner of walled fishtown area. SE elevation with viewing balcony supported on metal joists; segmental-arched bipartite window at ground, glazed, projecting conservatory bay to upper stage, on slatted timber base clasping corner and extending onto balcony. NE elevation with slate-roofed lean-to to right at ground and narrow window above, with advanced chimneybreast to centre wallhead stack NW elevation with forestair to entrance. SW elevation with narrow window to each stage. Timber small-pane windows. Grey slate roof with stone ridge and attenuated finial to apex.

features.shortDescription: 7 FISHTOWN OF USAN, FORMER FARMHOUSE
features.reviewNotes: Imported from the HES national Listed Buildings spatial data. Statutory listing and location are authoritative; construction-date review remains separate. NRHE record linked by matching point location; review if it represents a distinct asset.
features.fullDescription: Early 19th century. 2-storey, 3-bay rectangular-plan house with projecting porch and single storey gabled extension to rear. Harled. Flat-roofed porch to centre of S elevation with 2-pane fanlight and window on return, windows closely grouped in flanking bays and above. Blank end gables. Non-traditional timber windows. Graded grey slates with cast-iron rooflights. Coped skews with block skewputts. Gablehead stacks. Good stone wall running parallel with entrance elevation to front.

features.fullDescription: Circa 1900. Gabled, rectangular-plan coastguard Life-Saving Apparatus House. Squared and snecked sandstone with some shallow, bull-faced dressings. Depressed arch garage door to NE gable with 2-leaf boarded doors. Segmental-headed windows to long elevations, timber small-pane bipartite. Timber bargeboards. Blue slate roof.

features.fullDescription: Earlier 19th century. Pair of single storey, 3-bay traditional cottages, beginning a longer later terrace. Rubble with ashlar dressings, droved to later window detailing, harl pointing. Each cottage with door to centre of SE elevation with 2-pane fanlights and flanking windows. Projections to rear. Timber 4-pane sash and case windows. Stone slates and coped gablehead skews. Brick stacks.
